source_review.notes: Checked all thirteen primary or project-authoritative references. Current CNCF guidance supports user-defined capabilities, self-service, secure defaults, and golden-path compositions. Current Backstage documentation supports schema-driven templates, ordered actions, review, task identity/status, permissions over tasks/parameters/steps/actions, dry-run support that custom actions must implement and test, and audit events for task operations. Backstage's system model supports component/API/resource/system/group relationships. GitHub documents that repository templates copy files into new repositories with unrelated history, supporting the non-propagation warning. SLSA v1.2 defines provenance as verifiable production-origin information without making it current conformance. NIST SSDF supports integrating secure practices into the lifecycle. OpenSSF Scorecard documents bounded automated source/build/dependency/maintenance checks. JSON Schema and OpenGitOps support typed validation and versioned declarative state.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can define terminal outcomes and specifications, validate secret-free intent, authorize bounded actions, persist/reconcile partial state, minimize seeds, bind platform capabilities, protect the supply chain, test the complete journey, upgrade present consumers, import brownfield services, operate the scaffolder, and retire templates safely.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence progresses from terminal outcome/specification through inputs/secrets/authorization, action graphs/partial failure/provenance, seeds/ownership/catalog/source/build/runtime bindings, experience/testing/dry run, upgrades/conformance/brownfield, operations/portfolio, and retirement. Ten examples cover fleet drift, secret persistence, unknown outcomes, injection, terminal evidence, propagation, overwrite, dry-run bounds, portfolio sprawl, and brownfield adoption. Five exercises progress from definitions through end-to-end design, adversarial correction, portfolio architecture, and compromise response, with complete model answers.
